newsitem.title: CANADA: Agriculture Canada invites industry research funds.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture Canada invites industry research funds.

text.p: Agriculture Canada invited firms on Friday to offer matching funds to set the research agenda at Ag Canada labs.

"This is an opportunity for you as an industry to show us what your real research priorities are," Agriculture Canada deputy minister Frank Claydon told delegates at the Canada Grains Council in Ottawa.
Ag Canada has 18 labs which have seen "phenomenal growth in matching investments since 1991," Claydon said.
Quaker Oats Co is currently sponsoring genetic studies on oats with one Ag Canada research center, he noted.
Ten other firms have invested C$22,000 a year each to fund research by a team of scientists to "advance access to new proprietary identity preserved" oilseed genetics, Claydon said.
Three other firms are considering investing in the Saskatoon-based research project, he said.
Transgenic canola, canola that has been genetically altered to be herbicide or pesticide resistant, was recently approved for import into Japan but has not yet gained regulatory approval in Europe.
"It (European access) is something we're working away at but I don't know when (it might be approved)," Claydon said.
Ag Canada is also developing new varieties of feed and malting barley with a view to expanding Asian market share.
Meanwhile, Canada is seeking greater access to markets such as South Korea for its feed and malt barley as well as soybeans.
"South Korea's soybean tariff is unacceptably high," Claydon said.
"We remain unsatisfied with the European Union's import regime on grains which we feel are inconsistent with their World Trade Organization commitments," Claydon added.
